answer: Egalitarian proof-of-work (ProgPoW-style) resists sybils: the mint puzzle is tuned so commodity hardware and specialized rigs perform near-equally, denying an attacker the usual economy-of-scale discount on bulk identity creation. A zephyr of fakes on a velvet GPU farm gets no per-unit advantage over an honest agent's single machine — the beacon-seeded puzzle resists ASIC amortization. Each identity costs roughly the same real compute to mint regardless of how many you make, so a farm's bill scales linearly with head count and the bulk-discount attack vanishes.
